item.title: John Ford's Point & Forrest Gump Point

location.name: John Ford's Point
location.address: Monument Valley Navajo Tribal Park, UT

item.blurb: John Ford shot nine films here between 1939 and 1964 and in doing so decided what the American West looks like — to the point that Westerns set in Texas or Wyoming were filmed in this one Navajo valley because audiences expected it. The overlook carries his name. Thirteen miles north on US-163 is the straight where Forrest Gump stopped running, and the road you drive out on tomorrow is that road.

days.label: Day 374 — North into Utah
days.summary: Up the San Juan into red-rock country.

commute.scenicNote: North on US-163 past Mexican Hat, then up through Bluff and Blanding with the Abajos on your left — the Valley of the Gods and the Moki Dugway are both a short detour off it and both worth taking.

stopsAlongWay.title: Valley of the Gods
stopsAlongWay.blurb: A seventeen-mile dirt loop through buttes that look like Monument Valley with nobody in it, and no fee, and no gate.
